data.title: JetBlue Expands Fort Lauderdale's International Network with New Flights to Honduras and Grand Cayman
data.description:
JetBlue () today announced the next phase of its continued expansion at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL), with flights now on sale for two new daily nonstop international routes to Comayagua, Honduras, home to Palmerola International Airport (XPL), which serves the capital city of Tegucigalpa; and George Town, Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, via Owen Roberts International Airport (GCM).¹

Tegucigalpa will be a brand-new destination for JetBlue and its second in Honduras, further strengthening the airline’s growing network across Latin America and the Caribbean.

Flights to Grand Cayman will begin February 23, 2027, followed by Tegucigalpa on February 25. JetBlue will also offer limited-time daily nonstop service between Fort Lauderdale and Port of Spain from January 29 through February 15, giving customers a convenient option to travel to Trinidad and Tobago for the country's popular Carnival celebrations.¹

“We're grateful for the way customers across South Florida continue to embrace JetBlue, and we're committed to delivering even more of the destinations and travel options they're looking for,” said Daniel Shurz, senior vice president, revenue, network and enterprise planning, JetBlue. “With new international service to Honduras and Grand Cayman, we're strengthening Fort Lauderdale's role as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, making it easier for customers to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places and travel across our growing network.”

Growing JetBlue's International Network from Fort Lauderdale

The new routes build on JetBlue's continued investment in Fort Lauderdale as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, following the recent launch of service to Barranquilla and Cali, Colombia. By the end of February 2027, with the addition of Grand Cayman and Tegucigalpa, JetBlue will offer nonstop service from Fort Lauderdale to 20 international destinations, providing South Florida travelers with more options while strengthening regional connectivity and expanding the airline's international network. The new routes will also provide convenient connections through Fort Lauderdale to additional destinations across JetBlue's network.

New service to Tegucigalpa expands JetBlue's presence in Honduras, complementing existing flights between Fort Lauderdale and San Pedro Sula. Meanwhile, Grand Cayman adds another nonstop option to one of the Caribbean's most popular leisure destinations.

JetBlue expects to operate more than 150 daily departures from Fort Lauderdale during peak periods this winter, its largest schedule ever at FLL. The continued growth supports the airline's JetForward strategy to build a stronger, more connected network while delivering the destinations, products and perks customers value.

The JetBlue Experience

JetBlue plans to operate the new routes with its Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft. Customers can enjoy the airline's signature Main customer experience, including fast, free, unlimited Fly-Fi®, seatback entertainment at every seat, and complimentary snacks and drinks.²

EvenMore customers enjoy added benefits including extra legroom, priority security where available, early boarding, dedicated overhead bin space and additional onboard perks.

To celebrate the launch of its new international service, JetBlue is offering special introductory one-way fares from Fort Lauderdale to Tegucigalpa and Grand Cayman, giving customers even more reasons to explore new destinations, reconnect with family and friends, and experience JetBlue's award-winning service.

data.title: Canada Producer Prices Rise Again in October, Buoyed by Energy Products
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian manufactured goods prices continued to climb last month as the Iran war again drove up energy and petroleum products.

Statistics Canada's industrial product price index increased 0.3% in October from the month before, a softer advance than the upwardly revised 1.5% rise that in September. Compared with a year earlier, prices were 12.6% higher, a 25th consecutive annual increase.

Still, prices for raw materials bought by manufacturers operating in the country fell 1% in the latest month, though were up 23.5% compared with last year.

The steady rise in producer prices adds to signs of cost pressures since the start of the Iran conflict, which has elevated prices for crude oil and other commodities and added to economic uncertainty.

Prices for energy and petroleum products in Canada increased 1.2% in October after an 8.6% gain in September. Excluding energy, industrial product prices edged up 0.1% during October and were 6.7% above the same month last year, the national data agency said.

A rise in diesel fuel prices drove the increase, followed by light fuel oils, while finished motor gasoline prices declined 1.2% and helped moderate the advance in energy. Compared with a year prior, diesel fuel increased 93.3%, gasoline was up 50.2%, and light fuel oils climbed 100.3%.

Prices also rose month-on-month for chemicals and chemical products, and for fabricated metal products and construction materials, Statistics Canada said. There was a drop in prices for primary non-ferrous and primary ferrous metals.

The industrial product price index measures the prices that manufacturers in Canada receive once their goods leave the plant. It doesn't reflect the final prices consumers pay for goods on store shelves.

Consumer price inflation has been at or above the upper end of the Bank of Canada's 1%-to-3% control range for the last four months, holding at 3.1% in October. The central bank has increasingly focused on the rise in the outlook for inflation, and has forecast that annual inflation will accelerate to 3.5% by the end of the year and remain above 3% through much of 2028 before gradually cooling.

Worries that elevated energy prices will spread through the economy more broadly prompted the bank to lifts its policy interest rate in late October. Deputy Gov. Toni Gravelle in a speech this week said the longer oil prices remain high the less likely it is companies won't pass that along, and already there have been signs of that spillover.

The consumer-price index and industrial product data are the last inflation gauges the Bank of Canada's governing council will see before its next policy meeting on Dec. 9.

Prices for raw materials in Canada, which track costs paid by manufacturers, were driven down in October by metal ores, concentrates and scrap. This offset a rise in crude energy products costs. excluding crude energy products, raw materials costs fell by 3.3% between September and October.

The fall in ores, concentrates and scrap was led by lower prices for gold, silver and platinum group metals. Silver ores, concentrates and mill bullion fell 9.8%, while gold ores, concentrates and mill bullion decreased 3.8%, the data agency said.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: Most Gulf stocks retreat on Iran strife; traders eye Fed signals
data.description:
By Ateeq Shariff

Most Gulf equities closed lower on Thursday, weighed down by a flurry of attacks in the region and hawkish signals from US Federal Reserve minutes.

Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck by a suspected Houthi missile a day after Bahraini forces said they intercepted Iranian air attacks.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index fell 0.4%, hurt by a 1.5% slide in the country's biggest lender by assets, Saudi National Bank .

Dubai's main share index lost 0.2%, with top lender Emirates NBD losing 1.6%.

The Qatari index dropped 0.2%. In Abu Dhabi, the index finished flat.

Investors grew more risk-averse after the military action stoked fears of escalation, George Pavel, General Manager at Naga.com Middle East, said.

Fed minutes further cemented expectations of additional rate hikes, reinforcing the outlook for higher borrowing costs across the region's dollar-pegged economies, he added. Meanwhile, stable oil prices lent modest support to energy shares.

Saudi Aramco shares were up 0.2% after traders said fuel oil exports from Saudi Arabia were expected to maintain a robust pace, with Aramco issuing a fresh sales tender this week despite a refinery attack in late October.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting showed policymakers saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment.

Markets are pricing in a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike in December.

Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index was down 0.2%.

The International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday it had reached an agreement with Egypt to unlock about $2.3 billion in funding, pending board approval, as the country approaches the end of its $8 billion loan programme.

data.title: Walmart Q3 Net Profit Drops, Despite Sales Growth; Lifts FY27 Outlook
data.description:
BENTONVILLE (dpa-AFX) - Retail giant Walmart Inc. reported Thursday lower profit in its third quarter of fiscal 2027, mainly on the absence of prior year's significant gain on equity, while operating income climbed with growth in U.S. comparable sales and eCommerce performance. Meanwhile, Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth was slower than last year. Further, the company lifted fiscal 2027 forecast again.

In pre-market activity, the shares were losing around 1.04 percent, trading at $126.03.

John Furner, President and CEO, Walmart, said, 'We delivered strong results, growing our core business and gaining market share. The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.'

Looking ahead, for fiscal 2027, the company now expects adjusted earnings per share to be $2.84 to $2.89, with adjusted operating income growth of 8 percent to 8.6 percent, and net sales growth of 4.9 percent to 5.2 percent, all in constant currency.

Walmart previously projected adjusted earnings per share to be $2.80 to $2.87, with adjusted operating income growth of 7.0 percent to 8.5 percent, and net sales growth of 4.0 percent to 5.0 percent.

In fiscal 2026, adjusted earnings per share were $2.64, adjusted operating income was $31.0 billion and net sales were $706.4 billion.

In the third quarter, consolidated net income attributable to Walmart fell 19.5 percent to $4.945 billion from prior year's $6.143 billion. Earnings per share were $0.62, down from $0.77 last year.

The latest results reflected loss on equity and other investments, compared to prior year's significant gain.

Adjusted earnings were $0.65 per share for the period, compared to $0.62 per share a year ago.

Income before income taxes also were down 17.6 percent year-over-year to $6.744 billion reflecting 15.9 percent rise in net interest, while operating income climbed 16 percent from last year to $7.770 billion. Adjusted Operating income went up 5.5 percent at constant currency rates.

The company's total revenue for the period rose 5.2 percent to $188.835 billion from $179.496 billion last year. The growth was 4.5 percent in constant currency.

The company noted that timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days affected year

over year comparisons.

Net sales grew 5.1 percent from last year to $186.757 billion, and membership and other income climbed 20.3 percent to $2.078 billion. Membership fee revenue grew 17 percent globally.

Global eCommerce sales grew 17 percent, led by store-fulfilled pickup & delivery. Walmart U.S. eCommerce climbed 23 percent.

In the quarter, global advertising business grew 25 percent with 37 percent rise in Walmart U.S. advertising.

Walmart U.S. sales grew 3.6 percent to $125 billion, reflecting strong share gains across categories with continued momentum in eCommerce. Comp sales, excluding fuel, increased 2.9 percent on top of a 4.5 percent increase last year. eCommerce sales increased 23 percent, with strength in store-fulfilled delivery, advertising, and marketplace.

Walmart International net sales went up 7 percent to $35.9 billion, with constant currency growth across markets.

Sam's Club U.S. net sales were $25.9 billion, up 10 percent, and comp sales, excluding fuel, grew 4.9 percent, compared to 3.8 percent increase a year ago.

The company added that global inventory was up 8.1 percent, reflecting strategic initiatives, timing of seasonal events and cost inflation. Excluding Flipkart, inventory is growing slower than sales.

data.title: A key risk-on barometer is trying to turn higher
data.description:
Key points:
  • US equity index futures green; Nasdaq 100 rallies >1.5%
  • Initial jobless claims 203k vs 197k estimate; November Philly Fed 6.3 vs 20 estimate
  • STOXX 600 index off ~0.3%
  • Dollar dips; gold slips; US crude up >1%; bitcoin up >2%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield edges up to ~5.08%

A KEY RISK-ON BAROMETER IS TRYING TO TURN HIGHER

US stocks have been under pressure. The S&P 500 CBOE:SPX extended its losing streak to five sessions on Wednesday and finished 6.3% below its October 6 record close. The benchmark is still up 7% for the year, but that's only part of the story. Over the past six months, it has essentially gone nowhere, sitting 0.4% below its May 19 close.

The picture looks even weaker elsewhere. Both the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and the small-cap Russell 2000 have already fallen into correction territory. As of Wednesday's close, the Nasdaq was down 11.5% from its October record peak, while the Russell was off the same amount from its August high.

Against this backdrop, investors are searching for signs that risk appetite may be returning. One place to look is the relationship between consumer discretionary and consumer staples stocks.

The logic is straightforward. Consumer discretionary companies, which sell non-essential goods and services, tend to do well when investors are optimistic about growth. Consumer staples, on the other hand, are classic defensive plays that often outperform when investors become more cautious. As a result, the discretionary-to-staples ratio can serve as a useful gauge of market sentiment.

So far this year, the S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF is down 0.1%, while the S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Staples ETF has gained 11.3%. Notably, the ratio peaked in early January and failed to confirm the broader market's record highs in late January, early June, mid-August, and early October.

The ratio dropped to 1.721 on October 23, matching its lowest level since June 2025. Since then, however, the tone has improved. RSPD has gained 5.4%, outpacing RSPS's 2.9% advance, lifting the ratio to 1.763 on Wednesday.

That resilience bears watching. A ratio move above its 200-day moving average, now at 1.814, and then above its November 3 close at 1.820, could be an early sign that investors are willing to embrace risk again. A break below the October 23 low of 1.721, by contrast, would suggest defensive positioning is regaining the upper hand.

data.title: Carolina Complete Health Connects More Than 600 North Carolinians with Community Health Resources
data.description:
Fall Block Parties in Greenville, Asheville and Greensboro connected residents with local organizations and resources that support healthier communities.

CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- More than 600 North Carolinians attended Fall Block Parties hosted by Carolina Complete Health in Greenville, Asheville and Greensboro, bringing families together with local organizations and resources that support healthier communities. Carolina Complete Health, a subsidiary of Centene Corporation (), is the largest Medicaid plan in North Carolina, serving more than 740,000 members.

The events reflect Carolina Complete Health's commitment to supporting health and well-being beyond traditional healthcare. In addition to food, live multicultural performances, games and children's activities, attendees connected with community organizations offering resources related to food security, education, financial literacy, maternal health and other needs that can have a meaningful impact on the health of individuals and families.

"Improving health means looking beyond the walls of a doctor's office and understanding what families need to thrive," said Lori Keane, Director of Marketing, Communications and Community Relations at Carolina Complete Health. "These events bring that commitment to life by connecting our members and communities with trusted local organizations and resources that support healthier families."

Community partners participating in the events included Second Harvest Food Bank, TSCF Food Network, Unequal Shares, Pitt Community College, Unequal Shares, Total Maternal Health, Village Sis Doula, Cone Health, Triad Pediatric Adult Medicine, and the Greensboro Fire Department, YMCA Mobile Food Truck- Manna Foods, Catholic Charities, Auntie Eb's Family Development and Resource Center Inc., Pitt Community College, Contentnea Health, Pitt County Public Health, American Red Cross, Pitt County Department of Human and Health Services. Together, these organizations provided attendees with information, services and connections designed to address needs that can influence health and well-being beyond the doctor's office.

About Carolina Complete HealthCarolina Complete Health is a provider-led Medicaid health plan committed to delivering high-quality care to Medicaid, Marketplace, and Medicare beneficiaries in North Carolina. It was established through a unique partnership between Centene, the North Carolina Medical Society, and the North Carolina Community Health Center Association. Learn more at carolinacompletehealth.com.

About Centene CorporationCentene Corporation, a Fortune 500 company, is a leading healthcare enterprise that is committed to helping people live healthier lives. The company takes a local approach – with local brands and local teams – to provide fully integrated, high-quality, and cost-effective services to government-sponsored and commercial healthcare programs, focusing on under-insured individuals. Centene offers affordable and high-quality products to more than one in 15 individuals across the nation, including Medicaid and Medicare members (including Medicare Prescription Drug Plans), as well as individuals and families served by the Health Insurance Marketplace.

Centene uses its investor relations website to publish important information about the company, including information that may be deemed material to investors. Financial and other information about Centene is routinely posted and is accessible on Centene's investor relations website, investors.centene.com.

data.title: Belden Strengthens OT Resiliency Through Enhanced Systems Options Across Every Network Layer
data.description:
Belden Inc. (), a leading global provider of complete connection solutions, today announced the launch of new products and portfolio updates designed to help operators build resilience at every layer of the network, from the cable to the control room, with secure, dependable connectivity in demanding industrial environments.

OT networks across manufacturing, energy and transportation are being asked to do more: connect more devices, meet stricter security requirements and recover faster – all without compromising uptime or performance. Belden’s latest launches are designed to simplify portfolio choices, improve security and uptime, and speed deployment and maintenance. They also build a stronger foundation for IT/OT convergence.

Belden’s newest product launches and expansions include:

  • Belden Xtra-Guard™ Flex Cables – AlphaWire Xtra-Guard Flex is now Belden Xtra-Guard Flex, and the Belden MachFlex™ name is retiring in the Americas region. The newly unified portfolio features four families that match the cable to the motion for robotics, drag chains, tray runs and machine tools. AlphaWire part numbers carry over, and both distributor networks can supply the full range – so there's no disruption, only more capability. And it comes with real upgrades: a 10-year warranty, up from just one year on AlphaWire products; ship and debit now available for stocking distributors; and single 100-foot reels that keep minimums low for machine builds.
  • Belden OS – The Belden OS firmware provides a more secure, efficient and resilient foundation for managing Belden's ecosystem of next-generation 5G wireless and firewall devices. It easily connects critical devices via seamless integration to device management systems.
  • Hirschmann Operating System (HiOS): HSR multiple rings – This new HiOS release replaces dedicated redundancy hardware with native software on GRS2000 and BRP switches, following IEC 62439-3. Coupling two HSR rings via PRP once took four RSP or RSPE switches and now runs on two switches. Existing 2A and 3A sites can upgrade by firmware alone and PRP support is coming soon.
  • Belden NAC Software Updates 7.1.0/7.0.0/6.6.1 – Updated features to the newly renamed Belden NAC solution include the ability to configure specific domain controllers for the satellite server from the central Server page; library updates; and fixes for three CVEs. In addition, the NAC appliance was updated to the new Debian 12 (Bookworm), allowing for continuous security of the product itself. TLS 1.3 is now natively supported for 802.1X authentications. The latest updates also include method enhancements for the readout of FortiOS switches that use VDOMs and CoA enforcement through a special RADIUS disconnect method for Cisco Meraki.

Belden is also introducing the RailTuff™ Fire Resistant Ethernet CAT7 Cable for rail applications globally, along with the FiberExpress™ MPO Assembly Light Version and FiberExpress™ Fiber Patch Cord Short Boot for the Asia-Pacific region.

Collectively, these innovations help keep critical connections reliable, secure the devices that rely on them, and give operators the redundancy, visibility and access control to keep operations running. The result is a more resilient OT network with stronger protection, fewer unplanned interruptions and the confidence to scale.

To learn more about these products, as well as the technologies and applications they support, visit www.belden.com/new-products.

About Belden

Belden Inc. delivers complete connection solutions that unlock untold possibilities for our customers, their customers and the world. We advance ideas and technologies that enable a safer, smarter and more prosperous future. Throughout our 120+ year history we have evolved as a company, but our purpose remains – making connections. By connecting people, information and ideas, we make it possible. We are headquartered in St. Louis and have manufacturing capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia and Africa. For more information, visit us at www.belden.com; follow us on Facebook, LinkedIn and X/Twitter.

data.title: Clean Seed Secures U.S. Patent, Advancing Global Intellectual Property Protection and Solutions for Crop Residue Management
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    VANCOUVER, BRITISH COLUMBIA – TheNewswire - November 19, 2026 – Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd. (“Clean Seed” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has issued United States Patent No. 12,745,695 entitled “Residue Management System for an Agricultural Row Unit Assembly”, further to the Company’s news release dated June 16, 2026.

    The patent represents an important milestone in the Company’s intellectual property strategy and provides further protection for technology incorporated into its SMART Seeder MAX™ and SMART Seeder Mini-MAX™ platforms.

    Protecting Technology Addressing a Global Agricultural Challenge

    This US patent grant is particularly significant as it mirrors the Company’s international patent application efforts, including its Indian national-phase application for the same residue management technology. India represents an important market for Clean Seed, where the deployment of Mini-MAX technology is directly relevant to ongoing efforts to address agricultural residue burning and advance more sustainable farming practices.

    Across many agricultural regions, particularly in India, the management of post-harvest crop residue presents a significant environmental and agricultural challenge. Traditional residue burning contributes to air pollution and the loss of valuable organic material. Clean Seed’s technology is designed to manage crop residue at the row-unit level, helping maintain consistent seeding performance in challenging field conditions and supporting practical alternatives to residue burning.

    From Intellectual Property to Commercial Application

    The Residue Management System is featured on both the SMART Seeder MAX and SMART Seeder Mini-MAX platforms. Field operations with the Mini-MAX in India have demonstrated the system’s ability to operate continuously through heavy local crop stubble and demanding field conditions.

    These operating results are important as Clean Seed advances its international commercialization efforts, including manufacturing, licensing and strategic partnerships intended to bring its technology to agricultural markets where improved residue management and resource efficiency are increasingly important.

    The Company believes that its expanding intellectual property portfolio, together with its international manufacturing and commercialization relationships, provides a foundation for broader deployment of its technology and future licensing opportunities.

    ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD

    “Graeme Lempriere”

    Founder, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer

    Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd.

    glempriere@cleanseedcapital.com

    ABOUT CLEAN SEED CAPITAL GROUP LTD.

    Clean Seed is an agricultural technology company commercializing its award-winning, internationally patented SMART Seeder™ technologies. Designed for real-world conditions and backed by independent field trials, these tools reduce fertilizer usage while supporting higher crop performance and overall farm profitability.

    At the heart of Clean Seed’s product line is the SMART Seeder™ system—a breakthrough in precision seeding that combines advanced electronic metering with intuitive software control. Its ability to deliver row-by-row variable rate inputs positions it as a leading innovation in the next generation of sustainable farming.

    Clean Seed is partnered with Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd., the world’s largest tractor manufacturer by volume, strengthening its global path to market and large-scale adoption.

    The common shares of Clean Seed Capital Group Ltd. are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and trade under the symbol "CSX".

data.title: Lexaria's Human Study GLP-1-H26-7 Completes Dosing as Scheduled
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Kelowna, BC – November 19, 2026 – TheNewswire - Lexaria Bioscience Corp. (the “Company” or “Lexaria”), a global innovator in drug delivery platforms, reports that final dosing has been completed on schedule with Human Pilot Study #7 (GLP-1-H26-7) that is evaluating two oral DehydraTECH-semaglutide (“DHT-sema”) compositions against Novo’s® (“Novo”) commercially available Wegovy® tablets, over a 5-week duration (the “Study”).

    Final visits were completed this week by all Study participants within all Study arms. With dosing complete and final blood samples taken, the Study work will now shift to laboratory sample analyses, quality control and review of all data, and then reporting.

    No information from the Study will be provided to any third parties until all data has been reviewed and quality controlled. Lexaria will provide further information once that has been achieved.

    About the Study

    The Study is investigating three separate arms to assess safety & tolerability as well as PK properties that will compare SNAC-inclusive, DHT-sema compositions formulated in both tablet and capsule formats to commercially available Wegovy® tablets.  The Study is being conducted under fasted pre-dose conditions similar to the advised administration criteria of Novo’s oral semaglutide products. The 5-week dosing duration was selected in order to allow for achievement of steady state concentration levels, meaning that the semaglutide blood quantities in each arm will be expected to reach an equilibrium level that balances drug input with natural bodily elimination.

    The Study is exploring several new DehydraTECH™ enhancements not previously evaluated, which include but are not limited to the following two main improvements:

    (1) First, an oral tablet DHT-sema composition will be used by Lexaria for the first time, as opposed to only the capsule compositions administered in all our previous DehydraTECH™ GLP-1 studies. Novo’s Rybelsus® and Wegovy® oral semaglutide medications use specially formulated tablets designed to temporarily adhere to the stomach lining and disintegrate and dissolve  releasing agents in a focal manner that aids in optimizing absorption of semaglutide into the human body. For the first time ever, Lexaria has attempted to mimic and integrate certain physical properties of the Rybelsus® and Wegovy® SNAC-inclusive tablet delivery modality into its DHT-sema tablets to follow established industry standards and thereby increase the likelihood of subsequent commercial pharmaceutical relationships.

    (2) Second, both the Lexaria DHT-sema tablet and capsule test articles will be formulated with SNAC, which will be the first time these formulations will be evaluated over a multi-dose, multi-week time period in humans. The five-week dosing duration of the Study is expected to be long enough to reach so-called steady-state, which is when drug concentrations in the body reach a constant concentration.  As noted above, Human Pilot Studies #1 and #2 (GLP-1-H24-1 and GLP-1-H24-2), conducted in 2024 and 2025 which incorporated SNAC (but did not use tablets), were limited by single-dose study designs and therefore of much shorter duration.

    The Study is fully funded from existing corporate resources.

    About Lexaria Bioscience Corp. & DehydraTECH

    DehydraTECH™ is Lexaria’s patented drug delivery formulation and processing platform technology which improves the way a wide variety of drugs enter the bloodstream, always through oral delivery. DehydraTECH has repeatedly evidenced the ability to increase bio-absorption, reduce side-effects, and deliver some drugs more effectively across the blood brain barrier. Lexaria operates a licensed in-house research laboratory and holds a robust intellectual property portfolio with 70 patents granted and additional patents pending worldwide. For more information, please visit www.lexariabioscience.com.

data.title: Ventripoint Diagnostics Announces Placement of Two VMS+™ Systems for Clinical Deployment
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire - November 19, 2026 - Ventripoint Diagnostics Ltd. ("Ventripoint" or the "Company"), (TSXV:VPT; OTC:VPTDF) is pleased to announce the sale of two VMS+™ cardiac imaging systems, which will be donated in honor of Ella's Umbrella. The systems will support clinical research and the integration of advanced cardiac imaging into routine patient care.

    One placement is planned to support a study involving pregnant women with congenital heart disease (CHD). Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of congenital heart conditions, together with improvements in surgical and interventional procedures, have enabled more patients with CHD to survive and live longer lives. As this population ages, patients increasingly encounter life events and medical conditions, including pregnancy, that can place additional demands on the heart. These circumstances create a growing need for accessible, accurate and comprehensive cardiac assessment to support clinical decision-making and patient management.

    The second VMS+™ system will be deployed in routine clinical practice. This placement is intended to provide practical insights into how VMS+ can be incorporated into established cardiology workflows, including its potential to improve clinical efficiency, streamline cardiac assessment and enhance the availability of advanced cardiac measurements in everyday practice.

    VMS+™ utilizes Ventripoint's proprietary Knowledge-Based Reconstruction (KBR) technology to transform standard two-dimensional echocardiography images into three-dimensional cardiac models, providing quantitative volumetric measurements of all four heart chambers. The technology is designed to work with existing ultrasound equipment, potentially expanding access to advanced cardiac imaging without requiring additional investment in specialized imaging hardware.

    Hugh MacNaught, President and CEO of Ventripoint, commented:

    "We're pleased to see two VMS+™ systems donated in honor of Ella's Umbrella, an organization that understands firsthand how important advances in cardiac care can be. These placements represent an exciting opportunity to advance cardiac research and help more patients get the answers and care they need."

    "The planned study involving pregnant women with congenital heart disease is particularly relevant as advances in treatment continue to extend the lives of people born with heart conditions. These patients will increasingly experience life stages and medical circumstances that place additional demands on their cardiovascular systems. We believe accessible, detailed assessment of cardiac function can play an important role in supporting their ongoing care.

    "The second placement will allow us to gain valuable experience integrating VMS+ into routine clinical practice and better understand its potential to improve workflow efficiency and the delivery of cardiac assessment.

    "Both applications are consistent with our commercialization strategy, which focuses on targeted clinical deployments, building real-world experience and demonstrating the practical value of VMS+ across specific patient populations and clinical settings."

    Betty Mertens, Founder and President of Ella's Umbrella, added:

    "We started Ella's Umbrella because we believe more children deserve the chance to grow up. It's incredibly meaningful to see Ella's legacy inspiring opportunities like this, and we're hopeful about the difference this technology could make for patients and families."

    Ventripoint expects the experience gained through research and routine clinical applications to help inform future deployments and support broader acceptance of VMS+™ within the cardiology community.

    About Ventripoint Diagnostics Ltd.

    Ventripoint is an industry leader in the application of AI (Artificial Intelligence) to echocardiography. Ventripoint's VMS products are powered by its proprietary Knowledge Based Reconstruction technology, which is the result of a decade of development and provides accurate volumetric cardiac measurements equivalent to MRI. This affordable, gold-standard alternative allows cardiologists greater confidence in the management of their patients. Providing better care to patients serves as a springboard and basic standard for all of Ventripoint's products that guide our future developments. In addition, VMS+™ is versatile and can be used with all ultrasound systems from any vendor supported by regulatory market approvals in the U.S., Europe, and Canada.

    About Ella’s Umbrella

    Ella's Umbrella was founded in memory of Ella Mertens, who died in 2017 from an undiagnosed heart condition. Determined to help prevent other families from experiencing a similar loss, Ella's family established the nonprofit with a simple purpose: Keeping Kids' Hearts Beating.

    Today, Ella's Umbrella works to help save children's lives by advancing pediatric heart care through discovery, innovation, and connection. The organization funds promising medical research and technology while championing early detection to give more children the chance to grow up.

    For more information, visit www.ellasumbrella.org
